description:
RC4 provides code and structured data for “Benchmarking decision models against generative large language models on medical multiple-choice questions”. It is a release-metadata successor to RC3, created to trigger the connected GitHub–Zenodo archiving workflow. All scientific code, the analysis notebook, fixed configurations, structured data, methods, accepted numerical results and publication figures are byte-identical to RC3.

The study evaluated 13 decision models and 15 generative configurations on the same 1,273 four-option MedQA questions under closed-book, text-only conditions. Decision models had three runs and generative configurations one, giving 54 runs, 68,742 outcomes and 69,318 preserved initial/retry calls. The archive contains preparation and hosted-model collection code, scientific kernels, selected and first-attempt outcomes, native probabilities, resource measurements, retry provenance, Study Protocol v2.8, SAP v1.8 and presentation 1.51.

RC3 verification on 23 October 2026 used a fresh Python 3.14.7 environment on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, with all 102 pinned dependencies installed from local wheel artifacts. All 169 tests passed. Numerical recalculation reproduced the accepted scientific summary exactly, all 13 notebook code cells completed without errors, eight PNG figures and 15 CSVs were byte-identical, SVG/PDF comparisons passed after creation-date/document-ID normalization, and the interactive HTML was byte-identical. RC4 does not claim a new runtime execution. Its manifest and provenance/RC4_PRESERVATION.json identify the unchanged files and the included original RC3 verification receipt.

Reproducing the saved analysis requires no new model calls. Numerical recalculation uses the exact upstream MedQA test file identified in README.md; exact figure rendering requires the specified Arial font, obtained separately. Raw request/response bodies, reasoning text, credentials, upstream question/option text, a separate reference-key file and model weights are excluded. Selected labels and correctness can reveal reference answers; upstream MedQA keys are public.
